result.summary: This PR fixes a dead null-byte check in linearize-data.py caused by a Python 2 to 3 porting bug: indexing a bytes object returns an int, so comparing it to the string "\0" never matches. The fix changes the comparison to compare against the integer 0. This restores the intended behavior of detecting zero-padded block file endings and advancing to the next file instead of hanging.
result.problem: Users running linearize-data.py against a pruned datadir (or any dataset where the hashlist references blocks not present) hit an infinite loop instead of the intended 'Premature end of block data' message, because the zero-padding check silently never fires under Python 3. The author provides a concrete reproduction demonstrating the hang and the fix.

result.card: This PR fixes a one-line Python 3 porting bug in contrib/linearize/linearize-data.py where a bytes-vs-string comparison silently disabled the zero-padding check, causing the script to hang forever instead of reporting 'Premature end of block data' when a hashlist references blocks not in the blocks directory (the common case for a pruned datadir). The author provides a clear, minimal reproduction and notes this is the same fix as a previously closed PR (#32978) that lacked one. The change is a single line, ready for review, with no discussion or reviews yet (Crickets). It is a narrow tool-category fix affecting the small population of users who run this bootstrap-building script against pruned data, but the bug itself (infinite hang) is real and well-demonstrated.
